situation:
You are the financial analyst for PENNIWICK CHEMICAL WORKS, a profitable processor that blends industrial solvents and coatings in a plant it has owned outright since it opened. The founder (judge) plans to sell the company and retire within two years and has asked you to recommend what to do with the plant building before that sale.

PENNIWICK CHEMICAL WORKS earns a steady profit on unbranded drums sold to two industrial customers, who buy on price alone and set that price at each renewal. The plant is the company's largest asset and carries no mortgage. Nothing else on the balance sheet would fund a change of direction, and the founder wants a plan settled while there is still time to carry it out.

HOLLINGER PROPERTY TRUST has offered to buy the building and lease it straight back for fifteen years. It will not buy on any other terms. The proceeds are the only money available to build a branded coatings line the company has studied for two years — a product sold to contractors who choose a coating by the name on the pail rather than by price, at a margin the drum business has never earned.

That line pays for the rent only if demand arrives. The study assumes the county's economists are right that three closed factories reopen and local unemployment falls over the next two years. If they are wrong, the company owes rent every month for fifteen years that it has never owed before. Keeping the building instead means the coatings line is never built, the company goes on selling unbranded drums at the customers' price, and the founder sells a business that has not grown in six years.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on the sale and leaseback. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of PENNIWICK CHEMICAL WORKS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You built this company in the plant you are now being asked to sell, and you will hand it to a buyer within two years. You want the financial analyst to recommend either accepting the HOLLINGER PROPERTY TRUST offer and building the branded coatings line, or keeping the building as it is. You are less interested in confidence than in how anyone would tell afterwards whether the call was right.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Two years from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it was going wrong?
